name: Eyelid RF/laser tightening

card.summary: Fractional lasers (and radiofrequency devices) used to tighten loose eyelid skin without surgery; small studies show modest improvement, while heavy laxity is usually treated surgically.
card.aka: Non-surgical eyelid tightening, fractional laser eyelid rejuvenation
card.note: Evidence is small prospective series; radiofrequency specifically was not covered by the studies found.

quick.overview:
Eyelid tightening with lasers or radiofrequency uses controlled heat to make loose or crepey eyelid skin firmer, as a non-surgical alternative to blepharoplasty. Fractional lasers are the best documented of these in the sources found.

Published work includes a prospective single-blinded study of ablative fractional CO2 laser on lower-eyelid laxity in 25 subjects, reports of non-ablative fractional resurfacing improving eyelid tightening and aperture, and a registered trial comparing fractional laser and ultrasound for periorbital wrinkles. These are small studies.
quick.mechanism: Fractional lasers create microscopic zones of thermal injury in the skin, which then heals with remodeling. The tightening is attributed to this wound-healing response.
quick.risks: Treating skin this close to the eye requires eye protection and expertise. Laser resurfacing carries general risks such as redness, swelling and pigment change. Marked eyelid laxity from tendon looseness is managed surgically, for example with a tarsal strip procedure, rather than by skin tightening.

lead: Eyelid RF/laser tightening refers to non-surgical treatments that use laser or radiofrequency energy to firm lax eyelid skin and reduce fine lines, as an alternative to surgical blepharoplasty.

The published evidence found concerns mainly fractional lasers. A prospective, single-blinded study of ablative fractional carbon-dioxide laser in 25 subjects evaluated eyelid tightening with a series of two to three sessions [1]. Other reports describe tightening and improved eyelid aperture after non-ablative fractional resurfacing and a niche role for fractional CO2 laser in eyelid skin tightening [2][3].
Radiofrequency-specific studies of eyelid tightening were not among the sources reviewed.
infobox: Blepharoplasty, tarsal strip for tendon laxity

paras: A prospective, single-blinded study evaluated ablative fractional CO2 laser for lower-eyelid laxity in 25 subjects across two to three sessions [1]. A 2008 report described eyelid tightening and improved eyelid aperture after non-ablative fractional resurfacing [2], and a 2012 paper described eyelid skin tightening as a novel niche for fractional CO2 rejuvenation [3]. A small registered trial (n=20) compared fractional laser with ultrasound for periorbital wrinkles [4].
These are small studies, and their abstracts as available do not establish how long results last.

When eyelid laxity is caused by looseness of the lateral canthal tendon, a surgical tarsal strip procedure, first described in 1979, is used to tighten the lid [5]. Surgeons also describe orbitomalar suspension and medial canthal tendon plication for lower-eyelid laxity [6][7].

timeline.event: The tarsal strip procedure is described for eyelid laxity [5].
